questions.q: Q23. 23. The director asked whether it was me who had taken the final call on approving the budget.
o: who had taken the final call
questions.s: 'Be' verb (was) ke baad subjective case 'I' aata hai. Complement of 'be' should be in the subjective case 'I'.

questions.s: "Absent" as verb needs reflexive pronoun. Change "Randhir absented" to "Randhir absented himself" - reflexive pronoun required with this verb.

questions.q:
This camping site is a naturally sculpted amphitheater that serving as the perfect spot to lay back and count the stars.

o: that serving as the perfect spot
to lay back and count the stars
questions.s:
Correct Answer: that serving as the perfect spot

questions.q: Q7. 7. The 63rd edition of the Grammys was historic for Beyonce, which is now the female artist with the most trophies.
o: The 63rd edition of the Grammys was
questions.s: Insaan (Beyonce) ke liye 'who' use hota hai, 'which' nahi. Use relative pronoun 'who' for people like Beyonce.

questions.q: Q36. I am happy with ____ wins the competition. [NDA II 2021]
questions.s: "Whoever" serves as the subject of "wins". 'Whoever' यहाँ 'wins' क्रिया का सब्जेक्ट है।

questions.q: Q35. Q35. Abrahem also had one sister, of who not much has been recoded. [SSC MTS 06/07/2022 Shift-II]
questions.s: Preposition 'of' के बाद हमेशा objective case आता है, इसलिए 'who' के स्थान पर 'whom' का प्रयोग होगा।

questions.q: He is the only man I know ( who ) can laugh at himself.
questions.s:
After expressions like “the only man I know”, the correct relative pronoun is “who” because it refers to a person and acts as the subject of the clause “can laugh at himself.”
So “who” is already correct.

questions.q: Q36. Q36. Can you guess that of this vessels can hold the least amount of water?
o: (a) which of this vessels can hold
(d) which of these vessels can hold
questions.s: "That" is incorrect for a choice; "which" is needed. "This vessels" is a number mismatch; "these vessels" is correct. Option (d) fixes both.

questions.q: I enjoyed during (1)/ my tenure (2)/ at Shimla (3)/ No error (4).
questions.s:
The verb enjoy is transitive and needs an object. “During” already shows time, so the correct form is I enjoyed myself during my tenure.
Correct sentence: I enjoyed myself during my tenure at Shimla.

questions.q: Q39. Q[17]. The snake ______ we saw in the garden was poisonous. [SSC MTS 2022]
questions.s: 'Which' is used for non-domestic animals like snakes. सांप जैसे जंगली जीवों के लिए 'which' आता है।

questions.q: Gouri opened________ umbrella to avoid getting wet in the rain.
questions.s:
We need a possessive adjective before a noun (“umbrella”), and her shows ownership.
So, “Gouri opened her umbrella” is correct.

questions.q:
We really need to look at intervention who focus in long-term weight management that can achieve sustained weight loss at the recommended one or two pounds per week.

[СРО 16/03/2019 S1]
questions.s:
Correct Answer: That focus on long-term

We use "that" because it refers to interventions (things, not people). The correct phrase is "focus on," which means to concentrate on something. Also, "long-term" should have a hyphen as it’s an adjective.

Correct Sentence: We really need to look at interventions that focus on long-term weight management that can achieve sustained weight loss at the recommended one or two pounds per week.

questions.q: Madhuri and I have done my (1)/ work patiently and diligently (2)/ just for our safe and secure future. (3)/ No Error (4)
o: Madhuri and I have done my
work patiently and diligently
just for our safe and secure future.
questions.s:
The subject Madhuri and I is plural, so the possessive pronoun must also be plural — our, not my.
Correct sentence: Madhuri and I have done our work patiently and diligently just for our safe and secure future.

questions.q: Q1. Q1. Each of the researchers who were assigned to the international climate project were asked to submit his findings by the end of the quarter.
o: (b) who was assigned to the international climate project
(d) his findings by the end of the quarter
questions.s: The subject "Each" is singular, so the verb must also be singular. "Were asked" should be replaced with "was asked".

questions.q: On Saturday Rahul visited his professor to whom he had an appointment.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Is sentence me pronoun ki nahi balki prepostion ki galti hai. Appointment kisi ke sath fix hota hai isliye yahan par 'to whom' nahi 'with whom' likhna chahiye tha.

For example:- He had an appointment with his doctor.

questions.q: Her mother promised to / give her anything what she / wanted if she/ passed in the examination.
o: Her mother promised to
give her anything what she
want if she
passed in the examination
questions.s: Explanation:- Yahan anything pronoun ko define karne ke liye ek Adjectival Clause ki zarurat hai na ki Noun clause ki isliye yahan 'what' nahi 'that' relative pronoun ka use kiya jayega.

questions.q: Q32. Q32. The team leads, all of who had extensive experience managing remote teams, were tasked with training the new recruits.
o: (a) The team leads, all of who
(b) had extensive experience managing remote teams
questions.s: The preposition "of" requires the objective case "whom". "Who" should be replaced with "whom".

questions.q: The teacher said that(A)/ every girl in the class(B)/ must bring their own costume(C)/ to participate in the dance competition. (D)
questions.s: Every girl” is singular, so the pronoun must also be singular — her, not their.

questions.q:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.


I know a person who parents live in Milan.

[Stenographer Grade C and D 2024]
questions.s:
The correct answer is: whose parents

"Whose" is the possessive form used for people and things, showing ownership or relationship. In this case, it correctly connects the person to their parents.

The correct sentence would be: "I know a person whose parents live in Milan.”

questions.q: I remember / a friend to me / buying several pairs of shoes / at a sale. (SSC CPO Tier-01 23/11/20)
questions.s: The correct phrasing is 'a friend of mine' or 'my friend'.

questions.q: Theirs house is located on the corner of the street.
questions.s:
The sentence provided is incorrect. The correct possessive adjective to use is "their" instead of "theirs" before the noun "house."

So, the correct sentence would be: "Their house is located on the corner of the street."

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
o: whom she later married
which she later married
she later married
No substitution required
questions.s:
The correct answer is:

whom she later married

Explanation:

  • The word "whom" is the correct relative pronoun to use when referring to the object of the verb "married."

  • "Whose" is used for possession, but in this case, we are referring to the person whom she married, so "whom" is appropriate.

  • The other options are incorrect:

  • "Which she later married" would be used for things or animals, not people.

  • "She later married" lacks the necessary relative pronoun and creates an incomplete sentence.

Thus, the correct sentence is:
"She met my cousin, whom she later married."

questions.q: Both me (1)/ and my sister (2)/ went to a boarding school. (3)/ No error(4)
o: went to a boarding school
questions.s:
After “both,” we need subject pronouns when they act as the subject of the sentence.
Hence, “I” (not “me”) is correct here.
